import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from scipy.stats import pearsonr

# Select the most recent year's data (2015) for analysis
year = '2015 [YR2015]'

# Extract the relevant columns for analysis
education_expenditure = adjusted_savings_df[year].values
primary_enrollment = school_primary_df[year].values
secondary_enrollment = school_secondary_df[year].values
economic_output_exports = exports_df[year].values
economic_output_gni = gni_df[year].values

# Calculate correlation coefficients
correlation_primary = pearsonr(education_expenditure, primary_enrollment)
correlation_secondary = pearsonr(education_expenditure, secondary_enrollment)
correlation_exports = pearsonr(education_expenditure, economic_output_exports)
correlation_gni = pearsonr(education_expenditure, economic_output_gni)

# Perform linear regression for education expenditure vs. economic output (GNI)
X = education_expenditure.reshape(-1, 1)
y = economic_output_gni
model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)
coefficient_gni = model.coef_[0]
intercept_gni = model.intercept_
r_squared_gni = model.score(X, y)
